phase_0.boundary_condition: Input: arbitrary natural number N as decimal string. Process: encode N to both hex-digit IMASM word (tfactor read hex-digit) and native parity-graded word (tfactor read native word), run factorization on both word structures using their structural invariants (period, winding-commit cuts, dialect register U[9,25,32,35,40,43,52,54,66,72,76,83], crystal identity, type hash 16389838). The BCReentry bridge governs the atomicity decision: B-atomic (support4 cardinality 1) vs C-atomic (Nat.Prime), with the 8/13 reversal as the critical test case. Output: WellAddress (finite map prime→exponent) and binarySupport (Finset ℕ of occupied bit positions) for both encodings, with Γ/Λ interlace/deinterlace verification.

⊢.justification: the uninitialized value before any magnitude is recognized

⊣.justification: the closed numeral system that contains the complete factorization for both encodings

≻.justification: one step up in magnitude per bit-block, advancing the numeral

≺.justification: one step down in magnitude, used when halving via word structure

⋈.justification: chain a digit onto the numeral; composes bit-blocks sequentially

⊙.justification: the value recognizes itself at ⊙ after all bits are laid down

∈.justification: split the number N into its two atomicity readings: B-atomic (binary support cardinality) and C-atomic (Nat.Prime)

∋.justification: the two readings rejoin at the original number N; both are properties of the same N

⊤.justification: the affirmative arm: computes B-atomicity via binarySupport cardinality (support4)

⊥.justification: the negative arm: computes C-atomicity via Nat.Prime on the value

⊞.justification: holds BOTH atomicity judgments simultaneously at the 8/13 reversal where they disagree

⊡.justification: the WellAddress and binarySupport for both encodings are fixed permanently

phase_5.compiler_frontend: tfactor read emits both hex-digit and native words; native_numeral encode/decode translates decimal ↔ parity-graded word; native_numeral factor/unbraid/gcd runs arithmetic on the word's own bits
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: bit-blocks communicate via the native numeral's limb vectors (64-bit words); unbraid runs two concurrent arms on the same word; hex-digit tape carries nibble-level structure
phase_5.memory_mechanism: limbs_trim keeps minimal limb representation; word_bits reads bits directly from the glyph word; bits_to_value reads final limbs straight to bytes; crystal identity and type hash are structural invariants stored in the dialect register
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: encode writes bits LSB-first; factor peel runs small-prime trial division, then Fermat, then GPU rho, then CPU rho; unbraid runs two arms concurrently with Miller-Rabin on exhaustion; tfactor read provides period and winding-commit cuts as scheduling hints
phase_5.alfs_store: the ob3ect's own mapping word ⊢⊣≻⋈∈⊤⊥⊞∋⊙≺⊡⋈⊣ (period 14) is the canonical reference; BCReentryBounded.lean provides the B-atomic/C-atomic bridge; PrimeWells.lean provides the WellAddress type; tfactor read provides the dual encoding schemas with dialect register U[9,25,32,35,40,43,52,54,66,72,76,83] and type hash 16389838

phase_6.cycle_cost: one bit-block per bit of N (5 glyphs per bit for native, 4 glyphs per nibble for hex-digit); unbraid/gcd/modpow run on limb vectors, O(limbs) per operation
phase_6.post_cycle_state: WellAddress (prime→exponent map) + binarySupport (Finset ℕ) for both encodings; Γ/Λ interlace/deinterlace verified; period, winding-commit cuts, crystal identity, type hash as structural invariants
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — encoding is reversible (decode(encode(N)) = N); all arithmetic runs on the word's own limbs without BigUint intermediates; factorization reads the structure already present in both IMASM readings
